Review.Independence: A reviewer subagent that did not see the authoring conversation. It was handed contract.xml revision 1, the complete diff from 4de55c71 to 7e2d90d (40 files, 644 insertions), the four cited rule files, run-1.xml, run-2.xml and run-3.xml with the run-3 logs, and the output of grace5 status and grace5 check. It read nothing of the conversation and asked for nothing. Beyond the hand-over it read, because they are in the diff and bear on K1, A5 and the release rule: approval-1.xml of this change, notes.md, review-1.xml, the approval records of C-0007 and of the seven closed changes, the schema files, the source of check and close, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md; none of it was used as an account of intent. This review re-judges the whole diff from the start revision, not the fix alone, on the new candidate. Since CK2 filters its run to the AUTH and REL names, the reviewer ran the whole suite itself on this tree: 93 pass, 1 skip (POSIX-only FL-01), 0 fail.

Finding.Text: Two of the four conformance cases the Change enumerates cannot fail without the change, although it says each of AUTH-04, AUTH-05, AUTH-06 and REL-01 has "a test that fails without the change". AUTH-04 and AUTH-06 do fail on the pre-change kernel: an approval without Source fails approval.xsd, where Source was required, so check reports a schema defect and the AUTH-04 equality with no defects breaks; a rejected approval without a Statement fails that schema and never reaches the rule-8 phrase AUTH-06 asserts. The later test for an approved approval with no Statement fails there too, for the same schema reason. AUTH-05 passes as it stands on the 0.6.0 kernel at the start revision, because a Source-carrying approval always validated and nothing in the kernel reads Source, so the behaviour it asserts is not new; and REL-01 passes there too, because no 0.6.0 command wrote package.json or the pin either, so no command in that fixture can differ with or without the change. Both are legitimate regression guards against this change over-reaching and neither is a required check, but the Change's sentence, and any claim that the four listed cases evidence the delta, is overstated for these two.

No case exercised an approved approval with no Statement, which the amended authorization.md states as "the single word approved or is absent" and approval.xsd allows by minOccurs="0"; AUTH-04 wrote a Statement holding approved and AUTH-06 exercised a rejection only, so a regression that required a Statement on approvals again would have left the earlier suite and CK2 green.
Finding.Resolution: "AUTH an approval with no Statement validates and runs" writes decision approved with neither Source nor Statement, commits it, and asserts no defect from check, status approved, and exit 0 from start, run and close; the record is asserted to carry no Statement. It fails on the pre-change kernel, where approval.xsd made Statement required, so the gap is closed rather than papered over. What remains is F6: the case has no row in conformance.md.

Finding.Text: The fixture brief was the product-side half of this finding and is fixed: src/conformance/helper.ts now carries the template's own sentence, "Decision: approve, or reject with a reason. Approval is recorded separately and authorizes execution. A hold defers execution until the change or batch is explicitly started; it adds no kernel state.", word for word as models/architecture/templates/brief.html states it. What survives is the page the owner actually approved: records/brief-1.html:175 still says "Your words are recorded as you say them", which the change makes false, because the approval now records the decision and no quote. It cannot be corrected in place: the approval binds brief-sha256 9c7c44b7 to those exact bytes and no record is rewritten, so only a material revision with a new brief would remove it. The reviewer records it rather than letting it pass as fixed, and notes that no code, skill or document change can reach it.

K3 says "L-05 is amended and L-25 added ... no other mechanism changes", and the diff also rewrites the L-23 cost cell from "shipped with the change that makes it" to "shipped with the release that carries it". The mechanism L-23 records, the pin and the upgrade chain, is unchanged, and the rewrite is the same relocation of the step-timing sentence that the Change requires for upgrade.md, so leaving L-23 as it was would have left the ledger contradicting the rule; but a reader applying K3 literally sees a third entry touched, and neither the Change's list of documents nor K3 names L-23. The narrow reading is a defect of the contract's wording, not of the ledger.

The Change names "the review hand-over" among the documents rewritten to the approval rule, but the Handing over section of skills/grace5-review/SKILL.md is byte for byte unchanged; the only edit to that skill is the new Release discipline bullet under "What to judge". No instruction in the hand-over ever mentioned Source, a quote or the approval record, and the reviewer is still not given the approval, so nothing stale survives there and no edit was needed; the imprecision is in the Change's enumeration, not in the file. The prepare skill, in contrast, does carry the new decision wording.

The suite now holds a fifth new AUTH test, "AUTH an approval with no Statement validates and runs", for which conformance.md has no case row: its approval section lists AUTH-04, AUTH-05, AUTH-06 and REL-01 only. conformance.md requires at least one test per listed case, not one case per test, so nothing fails and the test is welcome; but the list and the suite no longer map one to one, and a reader of conformance.md cannot learn that the shape the amended schema permits, an approval with no Statement, is covered. models/architecture is inside Affected, so a row was available and would have kept the list and the contract's enumeration of four cases consistent with the code.

Review.Adequacy: bun run check is tsc --noEmit over src, so a pass separates a kernel whose types fit the new Approval.statement field, the Scenario options and the rule-8 loop, and whose new test file compiles, from one where any of them is the wrong shape, which exits nonzero; the log is the ts command and no error. It claims command-completion only, and type-checking is the whole of A3's first clause, so a pass cannot be produced by types that do not hold. It says nothing about runtime behaviour, which is what CK2, CK3 and CK6 are for, and a test that compiles but asserts nothing would pass it.

The log shows 12 tests ran and 44 were filtered out, so the name pattern is not vacuously green and the new case is among the twelve. A pass separates A1 and A2 from their failure: AUTH-06 fails whenever the rule-8 phrase is absent, AUTH-04 fails whenever the approval schema still requires Source, and the no-Statement case fails whenever the schema still requires Statement, because xmllint validation of approval-1.xml then gives check a defect and breaks the equality with no defects; bun test exits nonzero on any of them, and A2's claim that a closing change moves neither package.json nor the pin is asserted by byte equality in REL-01. What a pass does not separate is anything outside the AUTH and REL names, and AUTH-05 and REL-01 would pass on the pre-change kernel, so their share is regression cover rather than evidence of the delta (F1).

examples:verify reads the four example pages and contracts and the historical records of every closed change; the log names A to D clean, defective-brief reported as required, and the seven closed changes clean. A pass separates an approval schema that still reads the committed Source-carrying approvals, and a brief or page that still matches its contract, from one that does not: the closed records are validated against the amended schema, so a wrong amendment fails this check even though no example carries an approval of its own. It does not exercise an approval without Source or without a Statement, which is CK2's and CK6's part.

package:verify regenerates claude-plugin, openpackage, skills and cli-reference and compares them with what is on disk; a pass separates generated copies and a CLI reference that carry the edited skills and the new check rule 8 line from ones that do not, which is A3's second half, and the log lists each location ok. Its version rule is a comparison with package.json rather than a constant, so it neither masks a bump nor demands one; it would fail a version moved without regeneration, and it passes here because package.json still holds 0.6.0.

The command compares the CLI's own --version output with the literal grace5 0.6.0 and the pin file's text with 0.6.0, and exits nonzero on either mismatch, so a pass separates "this change is not a release" from a bumped package.json or a written pin, which is exactly A4; the empty log is an exit-status-only command and the script is in the definition. It does not read the README status line, which no check does, and a real release would fail it by design, which is outside this change. It proves the two files it names and no more.

The script names every directory in both locations, the two open changes and the seven under closed, and runs check on each, failing at the first nonzero, and check exits 1 on any defect and validates every record against its schema before rule 8 runs. A pass therefore separates "the amendment leaves the fifteen committed approvals, the receipts and the reviews of all nine changes valid" from "it broke one": deleting Source from approval.xsd, or making it required a second time, would make the thirteen Source-carrying approvals fail this check. The empty log is correct for a pass that prints nothing, so the script itself is the evidence of what was visited. It cannot separate a shape no committed record has, an approval with no Statement among them, which CK2 now covers instead, and it says nothing about behaviour.
Review.Rule: Read against the file, not K1's paraphrase. No record is rewritten: the diff edits no approval element anywhere, and I listed all fifteen committed approvals, C-0007's three, C-0008's two, this change's one and the eight of the closed changes. Every one still carries Source and a non-empty Statement, the single rejected one (C-0001-kernel approval-2) carries its reason, so rule 8 flags none, check exits 0 on every change and examples:verify calls their records clean. The binding is unchanged because readApproval takes decision, brief hash, Bound and the new Statement and nothing else, and Source is read by no kernel code at all; a Source-carrying record therefore reads with the same decision and the same binding, and a record without Statement reads with an empty statement that only rule 8 looks at. The amended file states what the Change says in the table row and in the paragraph that no longer claims the record quotes the owner or that review reads it against the conversation.

Read against the file. The change bumps nothing: package.json is absent from the diff and status reports 0.6.0, .grace5/kernel-version is absent from the diff and reads 0.6.0, the migration table rows are untouched after the new section, and src/upgrade/steps.ts is not in the diff. The new "Versions are releases" section says what the Change says, a version this repository tags, the previous release the nearest earlier tag, one owner-requested change carrying any number of closed changes, the four writes together, the upgrade verified from that tag on a clone with one open change; and the sentence that shipped a step with the change that altered the layout, the ignore file or the skills now ships it with the release that carries it. Nothing in the file or the code lets a change command write package.json, the pin or a step, which is K2's first clause as the file states it.

Read against the file. L-05 is amended to the decision record, carries the owner requirement of 2026-11-14 and keeps its removal criterion; L-25 is added with a source, the smallest alternative, the benefit, the cost and a removal criterion; L-23's step-timing sentence is moved to the release, which the Change requires for the same sentence and which F4 records as the one point where the literal reading of K3 is stretched. No other entry changed, no mechanism was added or removed, and every row touched still carries its removal criterion.

Read against AGENTS.md. The surface shrinks by one required element and one narrative field: Statement and Source both become optional in approval.xsd, Source as a legacy element the kernel ignores. It grows by one defect in check, rule 8, and by nothing else: package.json's scripts are unchanged, no CLI verb is added, no record kind or xsd is added, no migration step appears, and the two commits after the first review add only a conformance test and one sentence of a test fixture. The two new Rules lines cite existing documents, method.md's Releases section and upgrade.md, so "keep the surface to what the method document lists" holds, and each is one physical line. The approval line no longer asks for a quote; CLAUDE.md is untouched and points at AGENTS.md.
